concept.name: Circuit Breakers & Resilience Patterns
concept.tagline: Prevent cascading microservice outages by tripping circuit breakers when downstream failure thresholds are breached.

spark.summary: A circuit breaker wraps remote network calls in a stateful monitoring harness that automatically trips OPEN to fail-fast when downstream error or timeout thresholds breach, preventing caller thread exhaustion and cascading distributed outages. By failing fast, circuit breakers insulate upstream services and grant recovering dependencies breathing room to heal.
spark.keyTakeaway: The three states are non-negotiable: CLOSED monitors error rates during normal traffic; OPEN immediately fails fast without making remote network calls; and HALF-OPEN executes rate-limited probe trials to verify recovery before restoring full production load.

concept.whyItMatters: In microservice architectures, synchronous network calls block worker threads. When a downstream service slows or fails, upstream threads back up in unbounded queues, exhausting database connections and CPU, eventually causing global platform brownouts.
whenToUse: Wrapping remote HTTP, gRPC, and database calls in distributed microservice call chains.
Protecting caller thread pools from thread starvation and memory exhaustion during third-party API outages.
Enabling graceful degradation (serving stale cache, default values, or simplified UI) when dependencies fail.
Preventing the thundering herd from crushing an upstream service while it is rebooting after a crash.
whenNotToUse: In-memory CPU-bound calculations or local disk reads where network latency does not exist.
Write-critical idempotent transactions where operations cannot fail fast or serve stale fallbacks (use transactional outbox instead).
Endpoints where callers have asynchronous fire-and-forget message broker queues.
keyPoints: Finite State Machine: Transitions deterministically between CLOSED, OPEN, and HALF-OPEN states based on continuous error telemetry.
Sliding Evaluation Window: Monitors failure percentages over a rolling time window (e.g. 10 seconds) or fixed call count (e.g. 100 calls) with minimum request thresholds.
Half-Open Recovery Canary: Sends a limited trial batch (e.g. 5 requests) to downstream services; if all succeed, circuit closes; if any fail, circuit trips back to open.
Thread Pool Isolation (Bulkheading): Pairs with dedicated thread pools so that one slow dependency cannot consume threads allocated to others.
Graceful Degradation Fallbacks: Returns cached data, empty recommendations, or static placeholders when the circuit is OPEN.

examples.title: Recommendation Service Fail-Fast Fallback
examples.scenario: The ML recommendation microservice experiences a memory leak and response latency jumps to 15 seconds.
examples.outcome: API Gateway circuit breaker trips to OPEN in 3 seconds, immediately returning static trending items to users without stalling homepage renders.

examples.title: Third-Party SMS Carrier Outage
examples.scenario: A telecom SMS gateway returns HTTP 500 errors during a cellular network outage.
examples.outcome: Circuit breaker trips OPEN, immediately falling back to backup carrier routes rather than hanging client mobile verification prompts.

tradeOffs.factor: In-Process (Resilience4j) vs Service Mesh (Envoy) Circuit Breakers
tradeOffs.pro: In-process breakers execute rich application fallback logic (e.g. returning stale domain objects from Redis).
tradeOffs.con: In-process breakers must be configured in every programming language across polyglot microservices.

tradeOffs.factor: Failure Rate Threshold: Aggressive (20%) vs Conservative (50%)
tradeOffs.pro: Aggressive thresholds trip quickly to protect threads before latency spreads.
tradeOffs.con: Aggressive thresholds can falsely trip on minor network blips, causing unnecessary service degradation.

tradeOffs.factor: Stale Fallback vs Immediate Error Status Code
tradeOffs.pro: Serving stale cached data preserves user conversion rates during minor outages.
tradeOffs.con: Users may view outdated inventory or stale pricing, requiring clear UI disclaimer banners.

failureModes.name: Tripping on 4xx Client Validation Errors
failureModes.description: A circuit breaker counts HTTP 400 Bad Request or 404 Not Found as failures. A rogue user submitting bad input trips the breaker, knocking out the service for all users.
failureModes.mitigation: Configure the circuit breaker to count ONLY HTTP 5xx server errors, network timeouts, and connection reset exceptions.

failureModes.name: The Low-Volume False Trip
failureModes.description: During off-peak hours, a service receives only 2 requests in 5 minutes. One request encounters a client disconnect, registering a 50% failure rate and tripping the breaker.
failureModes.mitigation: Enforce a minimum call volume threshold (e.g. minimumNumberOfCalls = 20) before calculating error percentages.

failureModes.name: Thread Starvation before Timeout Expiration
failureModes.description: The circuit breaker counts errors, but the HTTP client has a 60-second connection timeout. 500 slow requests exhaust all worker threads before the breaker ever evaluates a failure.
failureModes.mitigation: Always configure tight client timeouts (e.g. 500ms) in conjunction with circuit breakers.

commonMistakes: Omitting a fallback handler, resulting in unhandled CircuitBreakerOpenExceptions crashing user requests anyway.
Setting the half-open cooldown timer too short (e.g. 1 second), immediately slamming recovering services with full traffic.
Sharing a single circuit breaker across multiple independent remote services.

deepDive.markdownContent:
## 📖 Operational Architecture of Circuit Breakers

In distributed systems, failures are inevitable. A circuit breaker acts as an automatic electrical fuse for software dependencies: when downstream failure rates cross safety thresholds, the breaker trips to protect the caller from thread pool exhaustion.

```architecture
{
  "view": "high-level",
  "title": "Circuit Breaker State Machine & Execution Flow",
  "nodes": [
    { "id": "closed", "label": "CLOSED State (Normal Operation / Error Counting)", "type": "service" },
    { "id": "open", "label": "OPEN State (Fail-Fast / Cooldown Timer)", "type": "route" },
    { "id": "halfOpen", "label": "HALF-OPEN State (Trial Canary Probes)", "type": "pipeline" },
    { "id": "fallback", "label": "Fallback Handler (Stale Cache / Default)", "type": "gateway" }
  ],
  "edges": [
    { "from": "closed", "to": "open", "label": "Failure Rate > 50% over window" },
    { "from": "open", "to": "halfOpen", "label": "Sleep Cooldown Expires (10s)" },
    { "from": "halfOpen", "to": "closed", "label": "Canary Probes Succeed (5/5)" },
    { "from": "halfOpen", "to": "open", "label": "Any Canary Probe Fails" },
    { "from": "open", "to": "fallback", "label": "Instant Fail-Fast (<0.1ms)" }
  ]
}
```

---

### ⚙️ State Machine Execution Lifecycle

| State | Request Handling | State Transition Trigger | Next State |
|---|---|---|---|
| **CLOSED** | Requests execute normally. Ring buffer records successes, timeouts, and 5xx errors. | Failure rate $\ge 50\%$ with $\ge 20$ calls in rolling window. | **OPEN** |
| **OPEN** | Requests fail fast immediately with `CircuitBreakerOpenException` or route to fallback handler. | Cooldown sleep timer expires (e.g. 10,000 ms). | **HALF-OPEN** |
| **HALF-OPEN** | Allows exactly $K=5$ trial requests through to the downstream service. Other requests continue to fail-fast. | If all $K$ requests succeed $\to$ **CLOSED**. If any fail $\to$ **OPEN**. | **CLOSED** or **OPEN** |

caseStudy.solution: Built Resilience4j / Hystrix circuit breaker wrappers.
caseStudy.impact: Zero global site outages caused by single service dependencies.

questions.title: Circuit Breaker State Machine Transitions
questions.prompt: In a Circuit Breaker state machine (Closed, Open, Half-Open), what triggers the transition from OPEN back to HALF-OPEN?

options.text: The downstream service sends a manual HTTP POST webhook to reset the breaker.
options.explanation: Circuit breakers use automated timers rather than external webhooks to transition states.

options.text: An evaluation cooldown timer expires, allowing a small canary probe of trial requests to test downstream health.
options.explanation: Correct! Expiration of the open cooldown timer moves the breaker to Half-Open to test trial requests.

rubric.excellent: Explains expiration of cooldown window and trial request probing in Half-Open state.
rubric.gap: Thinks manual restart is required.

questions.sampleSolution: After the open cooldown timer expires, the breaker transitions to Half-Open to send trial requests to test recovery.
questions.explanation: Half-Open acts as a safety probe before returning the breaker to full Closed operation.

constraints: App server thread pool size: 200 workers.

interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Wrap payment provider SDK calls in a Resilience4j circuit breaker with a 50% failure threshold and 5-second execution timeout. If Stripe times out, trip to OPEN immediately to route checkouts to PayPal fallback.
